Body: Addressed by #38184. V2 now discovers the account-specific Copilot API endpoint during device OAuth, stores it with the credential, and uses it for model discovery and inference. This covers Business and Enterprise subscription-specific endpoints without requiring the previously hardcoded api.githubcopilot.com URL. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #38227. V2 now accepts the known interleaved reasoning field names plus arbitrary provider-specific strings, preserves them through config and Models.dev normalization, and uses the configured field for OpenAI-compatible parsing and replay. The PR includes focused config, normalization, protocol, and generated-contract coverage. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #36336 and completed by #38184. V2 now provides GitHub and GitHub Enterprise device OAuth, credential-aware Copilot request authentication and required headers, remote model syncing, endpoint selection, and account-specific API endpoint discovery. That covers the login, per-request header/token handling, and base-URL requirements described here. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #35757. Location.Ref keys are now normalized before use in LocationServiceMap, so equivalent references to the same directory no longer create separate location graphs due to object-shape differences. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #35810. The V2 TUI patch rendering path and its diff aliases are covered by the merged structured-diff regression test, which verifies patch tool calls render through the intended diff surface. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #36336. The merged V2 implementation ports GitHub.com and Enterprise Copilot device OAuth, credential-aware request headers, defensive remote model syncing, endpoint selection, capability metadata, and billing metadata, with focused tests. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #36477. Malformed tool input now settles the tool part during the failing execution instead of leaving it unresolved until another prompt arrives, with the failure represented durably. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #37712, following the temporary UI removal in #36531. Runtime MCP controls are now exposed over the V2 server API, restoring the underlying enable/disable capability needed by clients rather than leaving a nonfunctional toggle. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #37291. V2 now enforces a subagent nesting limit in Core, preventing recursive agents from bypassing the guard and creating unbounded child-session trees. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #37523. The simulation input path now normalizes named special-key presses before dispatch, covering the named-key behavior reported here with regression tests. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

Addressed by #37714. The AI package now includes the image-generation domain and OpenAI image-generation implementation requested here, with the corresponding schema/protocol and tests. Closing as resolved on the v2 branch.

## Update: corrected root cause after further investigation

After the initial report was filed, OpenCode crashed again under the same conditions, but this time even CMD (in Windows Terminal) failed. This prompted a systematic terminal-by-terminal comparison that revealed the original conclusion was incorrect.

### Corrected finding: the divide is PTY implementation, not PowerShell vs CMD

| Terminal | PTY layer | OpenCode TUI |
|----------|-----------|-------------|
| Native CMD window (`conhost.exe`) | Traditional Windows Console API | ✅ Works |
| Native PowerShell 5 window | Traditional Windows Console API | ✅ Works |
| Git Bash (`mintty`/`winpty`) | Independent PTY, not Microsoft conpty | ✅ Works |
| **Windows Terminal** (any shell: CMD, PS5, PS7, Git Bash) | **conpty** (Windows Pseudo Console) | ❌ Crashes instantly |
| **PowerShell 7 native window** (`pwsh.exe`) | pwsh's own PTY, not conhost | ❌ Crashes instantly |

Any shell works when launched in a traditional conhost window (`Win+R` → `cmd`). The same shell fails inside Windows Terminal. This rules out the shell as the root cause and points firmly at the PTY layer.

### The database/zombie-lock was a side effect, not the cause

The WAL "corruption" and `disk I/O error` observed during Python-based SQLite operations were caused by zombie file handles left behind by any hard crash of the TUI. The database file itself was never corrupted (`integrity_check` always returned `ok`). The zombie lock binds to the **filename**, not the data — copying the database to a new filename bypasses it immediately. This lock is a consistent *aftermath* of the crash, not its trigger.

### System-level clues

- `sfc /verifyonly` found Windows system file integrity violations, which `sfc /scannow` subsequently repaired
- After SFC repair, post-crash **mouse wheel tracking leakage stopped** (mouse events no longer flood the terminal after crash), but the TUI crash itself persists in Windows Terminal
- `condrv.sys` (the conpty kernel driver) dates to November 2025 — over 8 months without updates
- The system has pending cumulative updates from 2025 that were never installed

### Working hypothesis (pending update verification)

The root cause appears to be an **outdated/buggy conpty driver** on this specific Windows 10 22H2 installation (build 19045.4170, last updated November 2025). OpenTUI uses terminal escape sequences that older conpty builds do not handle correctly, causing a native-level crash (no log output). Systems with current Windows updates have newer conpty builds with fixes for these sequences, which explains why this issue is not widely reported.

The SFC repair fixing the mouse-tracking leakage suggests that at least one system file related to console input handling was corrupt, which may have compounded the underlying conpty compatibility gap.

### Updated workaround

- **Use native terminal windows** (`Win+R` → `cmd` or `powershell`), not Windows Terminal or pwsh native windows
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1` reduces but does not eliminate crash triggers in conpty-based terminals
- `opencode web` bypasses the terminal layer entirely

### What removed itself from the picture

- ❌ "CMD fixes PowerShell" — false; any shell works in conhost, any shell fails in conpty
- ❌ "Database WAL corruption is root cause" — false; WAL issues were a side effect of zombie handles
- ❌ "PowerShell process model retains zombie handles" — false; zombie handles are crash aftermath independent of terminal type

These will be updated in the issue description if the original poster is able to edit it; otherwise this comment serves as the correction.

## Final update: root cause confirmed, resolved

After extensive debugging spanning multiple system reboots, terminal comparisons, and Windows system file repairs, the root cause has been confirmed and resolved. This is **not an OpenCode bug** — it's a conpty driver issue.

### Root cause

The crashes were caused by a **buggy conpty (Windows Pseudo Console) implementation** in Windows Terminal 1.24 and system `condrv.sys`. The terminal escape sequences used by OpenTUI (alternate screen buffer switch, cursor position queries, terminal capability queries) trigger deadlocks or buffer corruption in older conpty builds, causing the Bun-compiled OpenCode binary to hard-crash with no log output.

Key conpty fixes landed in Windows Terminal 1.25 (March–May 2026) that address the exact failure modes observed:
- **Alternate screen buffer loop fix** — no longer enters a cursor position request loop for applications using XTerm alternate screen buffer
- **Cursor re-sync after unknown VT sequences** — properly handles the DCS/APC/OSC sequences used by OpenTUI for terminal capability probing
- **Deadlock fix during cooked read with wide characters**

### Environment specifics

- **Windows 10 22H2 (Build 19045)** with `condrv.sys` dated November 2025 (8 months of missing updates)
- SFC found and repaired corrupted system files, but the core conpty bugs remained until the WT upgrade

### Resolution

**Install Windows Terminal Preview (v1.25+)** — it bundles an updated conpty implementation (`OpenConsole.exe`) that includes all the fixes. OpenCode TUI works correctly in WT Preview.

Stable Windows Terminal 1.24 uses the system's older conpty and remains affected. Users on Windows 10 should either:
1. Use Windows Terminal Preview, or
2. Use native conhost-based terminals (`Win+R` → `cmd` / `powershell`), or
3. Wait for stable Windows Terminal to reach v1.25+

+1 on this — same issue with the **oh-my-openagent** plugin scenario, where the fix is even more achievable because the vision-capable agent already exists.

**Setup:**
- Model: `deepseek-v4-pro` (text-only, `capabilities.input.image = false`)
- Plugin: `oh-my-openagent@latest` — provides `multimodal-looker` agent + `look_at` tool with vision fallback chain (`gpt-5.5 → kimi-k2.6 → glm-4.6v`)
- Action: paste screenshot (Ctrl+V) into chat

**What happens:**
1. TUI saves clipboard to `image.png`, `read` tool returns it as a `file` attachment
2. `unsupportedParts()` strips the image and replaces with `"ERROR: Cannot read image.png (this model does not support image input)"`
3. The model sees only the error text — no file metadata, no path, nothing to delegate
4. `multimodal-looker` agent and `look_at` tool are available but unreachable because the image reference was destroyed

**Why this issue's proposed fix helps:**
If `unsupportedParts()` emitted file metadata (`[Attached image: "image.png" (image/png)]`) instead of a hard error, the model could then delegate to `multimodal-looker` or call `look_at` — the vision pipeline already exists in oh-my-openagent, it's just blocked by the stripped reference.

**The broader picture:**
There are 7+ issues requesting auto-vision-fallback (#24948, #22828, #21004, #18437, #31936, #26160). Most were closed as `not_planned` or auto-closed. This issue's approach — *don't destroy the reference* — is the minimal, highest-impact fix that unblocks all of them without requiring a full auto-routing pipeline. A model that can see `[image.png attached]` can choose to route it to any available vision tool, MCP or oh-my-openagent's built-in multimodal-looker.

Verified the overlap with #33899 — thanks for surfacing it. Short version: #33899 does not fix #37946; this PR covers a superset of #33899's cases.

**#33899** (still open, unmerged) patches `ProviderTransform.message` in `src/provider/transform.ts` and injects the single-space text only when the assistant message **has tool calls but no text** — its guard is `if (hasText || !hasToolCall) return msg`. Assistant messages with *no tool calls and no text* pass through untouched.

**#37946's failing shape is exactly that untouched case**: an aborted turn persisted with only `step-start` / `reasoning` / `patch` parts — no text, no tool calls — replays as `content: []` (or `""`), and strict providers reject the whole request with 400. #33899's `!hasToolCall` early-return leaves it empty. (The two issues are also different failure modes: #33280 is a lenient proxy *injecting* a visible placeholder into the transcript; #37946 is a strict provider *rejecting* the request and bricking the session.)

Coverage comparison:

| wire message shape | #33899 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| tool-call-only, no text (#33280) | ✅ | ✅ |
| step-start split pieces (tool-call-only after split) | ✅ | ✅ |
| aborted reasoning-only turn, no text + no tool calls (#37946) | ❌ (`!hasToolCall` skip) | ✅ |
| assistant message whose only text part is `""` | ❌ | ✅ |
| string `content: ""` | ❌ (skipped) | ✅ (→ `" "`) |

Layer note: this PR runs the guard in `toModelMessagesEffect`, which produces the list later passed to `ProviderTransform.message` in the request path; #33899 runs inside `ProviderTransform.message`. If both were merged they would not double-inject (both check for existing non-empty text first), but one guard at one layer would be cleaner. Happy to move this guard into `ProviderTransform.message` with the `hasToolCall` requirement dropped — i.e. #33899's location with this PR's wider condition — if maintainers prefer that layer. Either way, fixing #37946 requires covering the no-tool-call empty case that #33899 currently skips.

Additional reproducible evidence from OpenCode TUI v1.18.2 on macOS arm64:

### Reproduction

1. Copy an image to the clipboard and paste it into the TUI.
2. The prompt shows `[Image 1]`.
3. Ask an agent to pass that attachment to a local image tool whose API requires a readable filesystem path, such as an img2img script.
4. The model may receive the pixels when vision input is enabled, but it has no usable path to pass to the tool. With a text-only model, `unsupportedParts()` removes the image before tool delegation as already described in this issue.

### Evidence

For clipboard images, `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx` constructs a `FilePart` with:

- `filename: "clipboard"`
- `url: "data:image/...;base64,..."`
- `source.path: "clipboard"` because no `filepath` exists

On macOS, `packages/tui/src/clipboard.ts` briefly writes `$TMPDIR/opencode-clipboard.png`, reads it as base64, and deletes it in `finally`. That temporary path is therefore not a stable, tool-addressable reference and is not propagated with the attachment.

Local session records confirm pasted images are persisted as image data URLs without a usable absolute path. This is still reproducible in v1.18.2.

### Impact beyond direct vision

This also blocks local path-based tools even when the active model can see the image. Seeing the pixels and being able to invoke `tool --input-image /absolute/path.png` are separate capabilities. `[Image 1]`, `clipboard`, and a data URL cannot be passed to tools that accept only local paths.

A privacy-safe fix could preserve file metadata for non-vision models and offer an explicit attachment materialization mechanism for local tools:

- If a trustworthy source path exists, expose it only through an explicit user action.
- If the clipboard has pixels but no source path, materialize them into an app-managed temporary file with a defined lifetime.
- Do not automatically inject absolute paths into remote model context, since they can disclose usernames and filesystem structure.
- Do not assume a local path is usable by a remote MCP server.

This overlaps #31221, which was closed as a duplicate of this issue, but adds a verified current-version reproduction and the local img2img/tool handoff case.

Heads-up: related PR #38270 (for #37946) overlaps with this one — analysis posted at https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/38270#issuecomment-5043908019.

Short version: this PR's `!hasToolCall` early-return does not cover assistant messages with no tool calls and no text (e.g. an aborted reasoning-only turn, which is #37946's exact failing shape — strict providers 400 the replayed request and brick the session). #38270 covers that case as well as the tool-call-only case handled here. Both PRs use the same single-space technique at different layers (here: `ProviderTransform.message`; there: a post-pass in `toModelMessagesEffect`). Consolidating into one guard — this location with the `hasToolCall` requirement dropped, or #38270's layer — would avoid maintaining two near-identical transforms. Happy to align with whichever direction maintainers prefer.
